comment: Every id a UI step may use: the string a control is tagged with, `.accessibilityIdentifier(...)` under gui/star and `Modifier.testTag(...)` under star-desktop/src/main (Layer 0, plan §6.2.1). Each client's unit test scans its own source for string literals shaped like an id in one of the namespaces named here (first segment of an id), so an id passed to a helper that tags the control is seen too; a Kotlin template such as "videoimport.format.${choice}" counts as the family `videoimport.format.*`, and an entry ending in `*` stands for a family. An id both clients carry is in `ids`; `knownGaps.<client>` names the ids that client lacks, with why. An id found on either side that is in neither list fails the test, and so does a gap that has been closed (remove the entry). A new namespace needs its first id listed here before the scan looks for it.

desktop.render.all.frames: Render All Frames is a menu item on the desktop (an AWT menu, which a test cannot tag); the gui's menu item carries the identifier. The button in the left panel that carried it is gone (D8).
